test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Fitter) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In the limit system, the distinction between allowance and deviation is:

options.text: allowance is used for single parts, while deviation is used for assemblies
allowance is the difference between the maximum material limits of the mating parts, while deviation is the difference between a size and the corresponding basic size
allowance is always positive, while deviation can be positive or negative
allowance is the difference between a size and the corresponding basic size, while deviation is the difference between the maximum material limits of the mating parts

solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Allowance:**

 
• Allowance refers to the intentional difference between the maximum material limits of mating parts, such as a shaft and a hole, to ensure their proper fit and function.
 
• It is a predetermined design parameter and is usually positive, signifying a clearance or intentional gap between the mating parts.
 
• Allowance is critical for defining the type of fit (e.g., clearance fit, interference fit, or transition fit) between components.

**Deviation:**

 
• Deviation refers to the difference between a size and the corresponding basic size. It indicates how much a specific dimension deviates from its nominal or ideal value.
 
• Deviation can be positive or negative, depending on whether the actual dimension is larger or smaller than the basic size.
 
• It is used to define the permissible variation in the manufacturing process and the acceptable limits of dimensional accuracy.
